cards.text: Jesus has just told a parable about a king’s wedding banquet (Matthew 22:1-14). Then the Pharisees, a group of religious leaders, go out and plot together. Their plan is to trap Jesus in His words.

cards.question: The Pharisees don’t show up themselves. They send their own disciples to Jesus, and who else goes with them?

cards.text: So the Pharisees’ disciples and the Herodians, supporters of King Herod’s family, walk up and lay it on THICK: “we know that You are honest and that You teach the way of God in accordance with the truth.” Friend, that’s a coworker telling you you’re the smartest person in the building right before asking you to cover their Saturday shift.

cards.question: The compliments keep coming. They tell Jesus He pays close attention to external appearance.

cards.text: Compliments done. Here comes the real question, and it’s about money and Caesar, the Roman emperor.

cards.question: They ask Jesus what He thinks. Is it lawful to pay ___ to Caesar or not?

cards.text: Big problem for their plan, friend: Jesus knows their evil intent. I once hid a burnt batch behind the flour and my kids found it in TWO seconds, and Jesus doesn’t even need the two.

cards.question: Jesus sees right through all those compliments. What does He call the people questioning Him?

cards.text: Then Jesus asks for a prop: “Show Me the coin used for the tax.” It’s like a magician going, “Anybody got a coin?” and the WHOLE room leans in.

cards.question: They bring Jesus a ___, the coin used for the tax.

cards.text: With the denarius right in front of everybody, Jesus asks whose image and inscription are on it. They built a whole trap, and He answers it with the easiest pop quiz in history.

cards.question: Jesus asks whose image and inscription are on the denarius. What do they answer?
Now Jesus answers their question about the tax. He tells them not to pay it to Caesar.

cards.text: Jesus says, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.” They plotted, they flattered, they asked the big question… and He takes the whole thing apart with one coin.

cards.question: When they hear Jesus’s answer about Caesar and God, they are amazed.

cards.text: So they leave Him and go away with an empty trap. Stick around, friend, because this story’s not done.
